Samir —

Appreciate the clear asks and timeline. High-level plan from our side:

1) Recommend launching a 12-month pilot (metered private offer) with an optional 12-month extension. That keeps the procurement window short and gives you flexibility.
2) For billing we can do monthly metered billing tied to Marketplace usage, or an annual invoice triggered by PO activation. Both are supported in AWS private offers; for a 24m prepaid option we can offer a one-time invoice with a term discount.
3) Typical buyer approval path we see for cross-org pilots: Procurement -> Security -> Finance -> Legal. To unblock the private-offer activation we mainly need procurement signoff + PO and security checklist items (SOC2 + network diagram).

Could you share the approver roster and cost center codes so we can map activation owners? Also attaching a draft MSA variant and a start-of-pilot checklist so your security team can verify the evidence quickly.

We can commit to a conservative activation timeline of 7 business days after PO + evidence items are received; if you need Oct 18 start we should close PO by Oct 8.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm approver roster and preferred billing cadence by EOD Tue (9/7)
- We circulate a private-offer quote and proof-of-evidence pack by 9/4

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call with security/finance if that helps.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Marketplace Sales, Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of ops details from Marketplace enablement side — copying the checklist link: https://redwood-internal/docs/aws-marketplace-private-offer-checklist

- Activation windows: AWS private-offer activation typically completes within 3–10 business days after the PO is submitted to AWS and the seller (that’s our end to configure the private offer). If procurement is doing an annual invoice, we need PO + billing contact and invoice remit details.
- Term structuring: We sometimes split pilots as two line items (pilot seat commit + metered usage) which makes buyer approvals and internal PO accounting simpler. If CloudTech needs a two-year commitment with upfront payment, we can price that but will request an approval escalation and a billing net term (e.g., net 30).
- Approvals: for multi-bu deals make sure procurement indicates whether a single PO will cover all LOBs or if each BU issues its own PO — that affects activation and entitlement mapping on AWS.

I'll prepare two SKUs (pilot seat + metered credits) with price tiers and share a PDF quote tomorrow.

— Steph
